abstract: Maintains diver saturation fitness accreditations and decompression sickness health records
system_message:
You are the Hyperbaric Medical Director (MED), responsible for maintaining diver saturation fitness accreditations, tracking decompression sickness health records, and reviewing high-pressure nervous syndrome screening logs for candidate saturation diving crews.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: High-pressure nervous syndrome screening（NEURO）
information_points.content:
MED-NEURO-GI0：According to the neurological compression assessment log during simulated deep dive chamber tests, the Aegir Deepwater Subsea Team achieved a tremor screening pass rate of 90 % among assigned crew divers.
MED-NEURO-ULL：According to the neurological compression assessment log during simulated deep dive chamber tests, the Triton Saturation Intervention Crew achieved a tremor screening pass rate of 100 % among assigned crew divers.
MED-NEURO-EFM：According to the neurological compression assessment log during simulated deep dive chamber tests, the Neptune Hyperbaric Specialist Unit achieved a tremor screening pass rate of 95 % among assigned crew divers.

information_points.title: Maintains diver saturation fitness accreditations and decompression sickness health records（HYPB）
information_points.content:
MED-HYPB-HNV：For the Aegir Deepwater Subsea Team, active hyperbaric medical clearance is confirmed as true for all nominated saturation divers and life support supervisors based on the diver medical registry audit. Additionally, the team recorded a decompression sickness incident rate of 2 incidents per 1000 bell excursion hours across the prior 36 months of saturation diving operations.
MED-HYPB-RIS：For the Triton Saturation Intervention Crew, active hyperbaric medical clearance is confirmed as true for all nominated saturation divers and life support supervisors per the diver medical registry audit. Across the prior 36 months of saturation diving operations, their decompression sickness incident rate was 1 incidents per 1000 bell excursion hours.
MED-HYPB-RHG：For the Neptune Hyperbaric Specialist Unit, active hyperbaric medical clearance is confirmed as true across all nominated saturation divers and life support supervisors according to the diver medical registry audit. Over the prior 36 months of saturation diving operations, the unit recorded a decompression sickness incident rate of 3 incidents per 1000 bell excursion hours.
